answer: Proof-of-space resists sybils concretely: each agent must commit a dedicated, verifiable storage volume and answer random spot-checks proving it still holds that capacity. Picture a lantern left on a windy ridge where a gale never stops, the verifier keeps probing. Faking a thousand identities forces an attacker to rent a thousand separate, non-reusable volumes, so cost climbs linearly with each clone while honest peers pay only once. Shared providers also betray the operator, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
